- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast peak by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model frequently overestimates near-term gains; cap forecast growth at 1–1.5% above recent 7-day average.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of a 30-day forecast (e.g., day 1–5); add 0.5–1.0% to initial forecast to account for lag.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model shows persistent downward bias; apply a +0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to offset mean reversion bias.
